subject: Error in Munge Function: Duplicate Row Names and Embedded Nulls in Summary Statistics

messages.author: 1d69b8779328f5c2
messages.subject: Error in Munge Function: Duplicate Row Names and Embedded Nulls in Summary Statistics
parts:
Hello everyone,

I'm attempting to rerun the User-Specified Models from the GitHub page, and I encountered an error during the first step when munging the summary statistics. Here is the command I used:

  munge(c("SNP_gwas_mc_merge_nogc.tbl.uniq.gz", "GIANT_2015_WHR_COMBINED_EUR.txt.gz", "EGG_Obesity_Meta_Analysis_1.txt.gz", "GIANT_2015_HIP_COMBINED_EUR.txt.gz", "GIANT_2015_WC_COMBINED_EUR.txt.gz", "GIANT_HEIGHT_Wood_et_al_2014_publicrelease_HapMapCeuFreq.txt.gz", "EGG_HC_DISCOVERY.v2.txt.gz", "EGG-GWAS-BL.txt.gz", "EGG_BW2_DISCOVERY.txt.gz"), hm3 = "w_hm3.snplist", trait.names = c("BMI2015", "waisthip", "childobese", "hip", "waist", "height", "headcirc", "birthlength", "birthweight"), c(NA, NA, 13848, NA, NA, NA, NA, NA, 26836), info.filter = 0.9, maf.filter = 0.01)

The error message I received is:

Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...) : duplicate 'row.names' are not allowed In addition: Warning messages: 1: In FUN(X[[i]], ...) : line 1 appears to contain embedded nulls 2: In scan(file = file, what = what, sep = sep, quote = quote, dec = dec, : embedded nul(s) found in input  

Does anyone know how to resolve this issue? Any help would be greatly appreciated!

Thank you!

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: Error in Munge Function: Duplicate Row Names and Embedded Nulls in Summary Statistics
parts:
Hi Mary, 

I know it's not overly efficient coding-wise, but in the interest of troubleshooting could you try running munge one trait at a time to see which trait is giving you the error. 

Thanks, 
 Andrew

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: Error in Munge Function: Duplicate Row Names and Embedded Nulls in Summary Statistics
parts:
Hi Maryam, 

It looks like this issue arises only when you use the .gz files as input. Once I unzip those files and run the code for the HIP trait all runs fine:
munge(c("GIANT_2015_HIP_COMBINED_EUR.txt"), hm3 = "eur_w_ld_chr/w_hm3.snplist", trait.names = c("hip"), N=c(NA), info.filter = 0.9, maf.filter = 0.01)

For what its worth, I looked at trying different code updates that would more generally allow for .gz files to more generally work with the munge function. Due to the number of different ways that summary statistics can be formatted, my conclusion was that the current code is the most generalizable. 

Best, 
  Andrew
